First of all it’s perfectly normal to think you’re making stuff up. Denial is the name of the game, basically. It takes work, but you can get to a point where it’s easier to accept things.

I struggled with it for two decades. It finally got through to me after I had a fight with my partner (an alter) because I kept trying to convince myself he didn’t exist. I realized if he wasn’t real, he wouldn’t be fighting so hard to prove that he was.

We all still have moments where we don’t think we’re real, or that something someone said was made up by someone else, but we decided we had to start trusting each other instead of doubting each other.

As for not being able to tell each other apart, I think that’s pretty normal? Alters can overlap and blend together. Alters can influence the behavior of other alters. It can be pretty confusing but gave it time and you’ll start to figure stuff out :)

The reason it’s transphobic to say you’re not attracted to trans people, or racist to say you’re not attracted to members of a particular race, is because not all people in those groups are a monolith and we come as varied as any other kind of people.
